thread.title_full: Two foreign nationals charged with fraudulent sale of 'Trump Bucks' to U.S. victims

author: empire state today
title: Two foreign nationals charged with fraudulent sale of 'Trump Bucks' to U.S. victims
text:
United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York, Jay Clayton, announced on May 13 that two foreign nationals have been charged with federal crimes related to the fraudulent sale of so-called ‘Trump Bucks’ to victims across the United States. The individuals, Goran Spiridonov and Kristina Janeva, are citizens and residents of North Macedonia and remain at large.
The case is significant as it involves a scheme that allegedly targeted many senior citizens by falsely marketing worthless financial products as being affiliated with former President Donald J. Trump and his re-election campaign. Authorities say these actions led to hundreds of thousands of dollars in losses for victims nationwide.
“As alleged, the defendants created a fictitious financial instrument and marketed it to Americans around the country under the false pretense that ‘Trump Bucks’ was affiliated with the funding of President Trump’s re-election campaign and other causes associated with the President and the Trump Organization,” said U.S. Attorney Jay Clayton. “That cannot be further from the truth. ‘Trump Bucks’ has no connection to the President, the campaign, or the Trump Organization. This fraud targets many senior citizens, taking advantage of their support for the President. We commend our FBI partners for detecting and thwarting this scheme. Importantly, this conduct may be ongoing, and we strongly urge anyone targeted not to provide financial information or funds to any entity related to ‘Trump Bucks’ or the fictitious products pictured in this press release.”
FBI Assistant Director in Charge James C. Barnacle, Jr., said: “These foreign nationals allegedly leveraged a false affiliation with the President’s administration to steal hundreds of thousands of dollars from Americans. The FBI continues to target fraudsters that manipulate our country’s citizens, regardless of where they’re located.”
According to allegations detailed in unsealed indictments assigned respectively to U.S. District Judges P. Kevin Castel and Lewis J. Liman in New York’s Southern District Court, Spiridonov and Janeva used online marketplaces and encrypted messaging applications such as Telegram from at least 2023 onward to market various fake products including ‘Golden Checks,’ ‘Membership Booklets,’ ‘Golden Badges,’ ‘Trump Dollars,’ ‘Diamond Bucks,’ among others under banners like “TRB” (Trump Rebate Banking System). These items were claimed—falsely—to be valuable legal tender connected with Donald J. Trump or his organizations.
Spiridonov is accused specifically of promoting claims such as offering $10,000 exchanges upon Trump’s reelection for certain purchases; Janeva allegedly marketed counterfeit certificates she claimed were issued by Trump’s business entities.
Both defendants face charges including conspiracy to commit wire fraud (maximum sentence: 20 years), wire fraud (maximum sentence: 20 years), and aggravated identity theft (mandatory two-year consecutive sentence). Sentencing will ultimately be determined by a judge if convictions are secured.
Clayton praised investigative work conducted by both FBI agents and Homeland Security Investigations personnel involved in uncovering this scheme.
The Office’s Complex Frauds and Cybercrime Unit is prosecuting these cases through Assistant U.S. Attorneys Nicholas W. Chiuchiolo and Jackie Delligatti.
Authorities emphasize that all charges remain allegations until proven otherwise; both defendants are presumed innocent unless found guilty.

The case is significant as it involves a scheme that allegedly targeted many senior citizens by falsely marketing worthless financial products as being affiliated with former President Donald J.
